newsitem.title: UK: Britain's "House of Horrors" to be turned to dust.
newsitem.headline: Britain's "House of Horrors" to be turned to dust.

text.p: Britain's "House of Horrors", home of husband and wife killers Fred and Rosemary West and burial place of nine young women and girls, is to be demolished and every brick ground to dust.
The local council in Gloucester, western England, said on Friday the destruction of the three-storey house at 25, Cromwell Street would begin on Monday.
The next door number 23 property, now derelict, has also been bought by the council for demolition.
To stop ghoulish souvenir hunters, every element of the houses will be methodically destroyed. The bricks will be ground to dust, every floorboard burned and every fitting melted down.

Together the Wests picked up girls and sexually tormented them, perhaps for days, before killing them, cutting up their bodies and burying them in their cellar or garden along with the ropes, gags and masks that restrained them.
Builder Fred West, 53, hanged himself on January 1, 1995, in his prison cell while awaiting trial on 12 murder counts.

Rosemary West, 42, is serving life imprisonment after being convicted in November of murdering 10 girls and young women, including her 16-year-old daughter Heather and her unloved eight-year-old stepdaughter Charmaine.
The demolition of the houses is expected to take around two weeks. At the end of the demolition a thick concrete "cap" will cover the cleared site.

"No decision has been made on the future of the site: nothing has been ruled in or out," council leader John Holmes said in a statement. "The demolition of the property is the best action we can take for the people of the city."
A survey company has been called in to carry out a public consultation exercise on the future of the site. The views of relatives of the victims will be the first to be sought.

Some local people want the site to be turned into a garden of remembrance for the victims. The money from the council's purchase of the sites will be used to look after the Wests' five youngest children.
One memento may survive, however, despite the demolition.

The wrought-iron sign "25 Cromwell Street" which hung by the front door and was made by Fred West, is still in police hands. They took it down early in their investigations to thwart souvenir hunters.
